topic.title: Cheaper to inject than to fix the canteen
topic.claim: We'd sooner buy a weekly injection than ask our office for a decent lunch.
topic.behaviour: Complaining about long hours and canteen food, then looking for a personal fix instead of a shared one.
topic.mechanism: Fixing a workplace needs a fight and an HR email. Fixing yourself is private, can be paid for and needs nobody's permission.
real_details: Researchers interviewed 79 urban adults aged 21 to 30 across eight metro cities
They found limited healthy food at workplaces and campuses is a major barrier to healthy living
Semaglutide's Indian patent expired on 20 March 2026
Generics launched at as little as ₹750 a week, or about ₹3,400 a month, though quoted prices vary widely by source
Insurance generally does not cover these drugs when used purely for obesity
topic.news_peg: Frontiers in Public Health study updated 13 October 2026, plus generic semaglutide launches since March 2026
topic.why_now: The study page was updated this month and generic GLP-1s are a hot topic in 30-something office circles.

score.reason: genuinely surprising, original pairing of two unrelated frustrations, anchored to current generic-GLP-1 news
score.best_hook: The canteen food hasn't changed in five years. But you'll happily pay twelve hundred rupees a week to inject your way around it.

problems: Slide 3 has 4 paragraphs; use at most 3.
Slide 4 has 4 paragraphs; use at most 3.

edits: slide 2: Keep the facts but make it read like talk. Cut the 'After its core patents expired in March 2026, dozens of Indian companies launched cheaper versions' sentence down to something like 'Then the patents ran out and dozens of companies jumped in.' Say that ₹1,290 is the lowest launch price (NATCO's vials), not the going rate, so nobody reads it as what everyone pays.

slide 3: The link between the injection and the canteen is never stated. Say in one plain line what the injection is for, using only what the sources support (these are weight-loss drugs), e.g. 'Bad lunch, tight waistline, so we reach for the injection.' Don't suggest it's a good idea. As written, a stranger has to guess what is being fixed.

slide 3: 'Fixing the office is a fight' / 'Fixing yourself is private' is a tidy, symmetrical pair, and 'So the canteen stays the same. We change instead.' sounds like a moral. Rewrite the last two lines so they are messier and more personal, e.g. what the HR email would actually say and why nobody wants to be the one who sends it.

slide 4: 'Everyone hates the canteen rajma and the samosas at every evening meeting' is broad and generic. Narrow it to one thing the reader can picture. Keep 'Maybe it was me,' but make it a little sharper or funnier.

slide 5: 'Cheaper medicine is good news. I mean that.' softens the take just before the ending. Cut it or move it earlier, and let 'we found ₹1,290 a month faster than we found one email for lunch' be the final line.

An editor could tell this was AI-written: Short, punchy one-line paragraphs with rhetorical turns that land on a polished closer ('Cheaper medicine is good news. I mean that.')

An editor could tell this was AI-written: Sincerity-signalling filler ('Maybe it was me', 'I mean that') and a callback ending that mirrors the opening: ₹1,290 for ourselves against one email for lunch

An editor could tell this was AI-written: Stat-and-brand details (NATCO, MRP, patent expiry) slotted in cleanly to support a tidy thesis, with Hinglish seasoning ('dekhte hain', 'rajma') added for local flavour

sources.fact: After semaglutide's core patents expired in March 2026, dozens of Indian companies launched cheaper generics, some under Rs 2,000 a month, down from branded prices above Rs 10,000.
sources.excerpt: dozens of domestic pharmaceutical companies launched lower-priced versions. | semaglutide's "core patents expired in March 2026" | price cuts of up to 48% | reduced prices on starting doses of its diabetes formulation of semaglutide by 36%. | Branded semaglutide was priced above Rs 10,000 a month before generic entry. | Some generic versions are now being offered below Rs 2,000 a month in some cases. | a drop of as much as 90% from earlier branded prices.

sources.fact: NATCO launched generic semaglutide multi-dose vials in India on Day 1 of patent expiry at an MRP of Rs 1,290 a month, about 90% cheaper than the innovator's brand.
sources.excerpt: NATCO Pharma Limited announces launch of Semaglutide Injection (multi dose vials) in the India market tomorrow | NATCO is the first company to offer Semaglutide in the vial dosage form. | Multi dose vials will be launched at MRP of Rs. 1,290 per month for 2 mg/1.5ml & 4mg/3ml | and MRP of Rs. 1,750 for 8mg/3ml. | Pen device will be priced at MRP of Rs. 4,000, Rs. 4,200 and Rs. 4,500 per month | approximately 70% cheaper in cost than the pen device and 90% cheaper than the price of the innovator's brand.
